outcomes.functional_failure: An original expected output or state assertion fails
outcomes.test_timeout: The official engine reports timed out after its configured per-test deadline
outcomes.harness_invalid: Extraction, instrumentation, imports or runtime probes throw before intended assertions
outcomes.nonreproduction: The two original cases pass under the original 5000 ms deadline; prior timeout cause remains unproven

prospective_extension.trigger: Focused original 5000 ms cases pass 20/20, but the full unchanged portable-fixture tree again yields 205 pass / 5 test timeouts, including both targets.
arms: Separate Windows process-tree sampler during a full default-deadline run; collect descendant counts only, never command lines or process paths. Observer overhead excludes this run from an uninstrumented latency comparison.

Dispatch all original 30 test files one at a time through the same official engine, with default 5000 ms case deadlines, portable virtual-merge fixture adaptation and unchanged hooks/assertions. Aggregate case executions and preserve per-file results.
prospective_extension.limits: A descendant-worker count plus a passing serial dispatch can support a suite-scheduling explanation, but cannot isolate OS scheduling, resource contention or engine initialization internally, and is not proof of a production bug or fix.

parser_amendment.reason: The first serial attempt stopped at file 21/30 because the metadata parser accepted 'Ran N tests' but not the engine's valid singular 'Ran 1 test' footer. The CLI case passed; this is our parser failure, not a native test failure.
parser_amendment.change: Accept singular/plural test grammar and add a regression check; rerun all files from the original private overlay state without changing deadlines, hooks or assertions.
parser_amendment.eligibility: The partial attempt is retained but excluded from full-suite comparison.

limits: Testing-budget sensitivity is not evidence that a production client bug is fixed.
Deterministic repetitions are not independent model samples.
No changes to authentication, account settings, system security or machine-wide performance settings.
No packet capture; no claims about all possible runtime traffic.
The study cycle retains its no-issue gate without a novel E3/E4 production case and independent review.
